Instructions: Is each candidate requirement (each row) out of scope or not?
label: out of scope
definition: provides information or describing facts rather than stating a requirement (e.g., “User’s profile contains their email”). This includes cases where a candidate is a caption that functions mostly structurally and does not encode any requirement, and cases where candidate is repeating the previous candidtate (e.g. prev candidate: only do X when Y; this candidate: do not do X otherwise). Statements of what the agent may or can do (e.g., "you can help users book flights") and descriptions of what a state means (e.g., "a flying flight cannot be booked") are information. Domain rules the agent must apply when acting, such as fees, allowances, or eligibility conditions (e.g., "each extra bag is 50 dollars"), are requirements. Repeating includes duplicating or restating a rule stated anywhere else in the policy, before or after the candidate (e.g., the same steps listed again in a later section, where only the first occurrence is in scope; a closing "do not do X for any other reason" after the allowed cases, or a general reminder of conditions each rule already states), and restating the whole policy (e.g., "deny requests that are against this policy"). A candidate that adds a specific case or action to an earlier rule (e.g., which requests to refuse) is not a repetition
